name: Ciwogai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Fittokka Gobak, Yakubu Danladi, Julius Dabet, Christina Riepe, Adedamola Aregbesola, Benard Abraham, Andrew Lewinan & Thelma Araokanmi. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the West Chadic North Bauchi Languages of Bauchi and Jigawa States, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-010. Dallas: SIL International. 123 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.3 'Phonetic inventory' (pp.22-24) covers consonants, vowels, prenasalization/palatalization/labialization; sec. 6.5.4 (p.30) compares Choogen Tsagu vs Choogen Dirya wordlists (final nasal); Appendix G p.64: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' 348-item Choogen wordlists are tone-marked, no stress marks. Sec. 3 states the only prior linguistic data on Choogen are Skinner 1977 and Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page ciwo1236 (Ciwogai); OLAC listing for tgd (Wayback 2022 copy); en.wikipedia 'Ciwogai language' and 'North Bauchi languages'; glocal.soas.ac.uk/choogen
sources.note: Catalog/stub pages only; Glottolog has 0 descriptive refs (5 overview/wordlist refs); OLAC lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List and Decker et al. 2022. No phonological content.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. Linguistic and cultural background to the North Bauchi region and the Wiihe people. Chapter prepared for P. Allsworth-Jones (ed.) monograph on Kariya Wuro; ms printout 8 Nov 2012. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Nothing. Table 1 lists Ciwogai (Tsagu) [tgd], c. 2000 speakers, Ganjuwa LGA; comparative lexical tables cite Ciwogai forms (from Skinner); bibliography names Takacs 2002/2007 historical consonant phonology of North Bauchi.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena. (T = Tsagu/Civogai, informant Dano Sheka)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2 'The phonetic inventory' p.5: o/e and phonetic vowel length (mainly aa) more frequent in T (Tsagu) than in the other languages; 'As for tones, usually three levels and a falling were heard in the recordings and a number of minimal pairs of monosyllables confirmed, but it would have been highly impressionistic to have included any tonal markings in the present work.' Comparative wordlist only.

sources.citation: Takacs, Gabor. 2007. The Afroasiatic background of the North Bauchi consonant system II. In H. Tourneux (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics III: Historical Studies, 103-131. Koeln: Ruediger Koeppe.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Companion to Takacs 2002; consonant system only, listed for completeness.

sources.citation: Takacs, Gabor. 2002. Outline of a North Bauchi historical phonology. Afrikanische Arbeitspapiere (AAP) 70: 187-202. Koeln: Institut fuer Afrikanistik.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only work with 'phonology' of North Bauchi (incl. Tsagu data from Skinner) in its title; historical-comparative and consonant-focused, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it is the one unread phonology item.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Dymitr Ibriszimow. 1994. Chadic Lexical Roots. Vol. I: Tentative reconstruction, grading, distribution and comments; Vol. II: Documentation. Sprache und Oralitaet in Afrika 20. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Second of the two works Decker et al. 2022 name as holding Ciwogai linguistic data; lexical only, would at most show tone-marked forms.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1974. A note on the North Bauchi language group (with map). Africana Marburgensia 7(1): 47-50; plus N. Skinner's unpublished North Bauchi field notes/recordings (cited by Blench 2012 fn. 2).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Skinner is the only linguist to have elicited Tsagu directly before 2020; his recordings had tone; any prosodic remark on Tsagu would be here if anywhere.
